decisions.reason: The 518 FLEX builds on the established and well-liked BASIC 518 and was publicly rebranded, so sunk investment and visible commitment remain high, and missing website evidence for 2020-2021 is more plausibly read as a pandemic-related lull than as failure.

The mobile high-speed grinder line had low visibility and no observed results after 2019, but it is a multi-model investment central to the firm's mobile processing strategy, and the firm already showed with B and E that it can cut parallel high-speed lines, so management would still justify keeping this surviving line.

The single electric fine shredder carries limited sunk cost and visibility, but it fits the announced resource-saving, electrified direction, so weak results would likely be blamed on temporary market conditions rather than on the product.

The stationary pre-shredder line has its own page and backs the firm's push into tougher stationary processing, so the strong public and strategic commitment makes management likely to persist despite unobserved recent results.
